notes: MIL-STD-1553B is a wire-level protocol spec; there is no OTP / fuse / configuration ROM at the protocol layer. Concrete 1553 Remote Terminal IP commonly uses straps or OTP to set the 5-bit RT address (often with a 6th parity-protect bit). Some RTs also use OTP to lock the BIT word, the Subaddress descriptor table defaults, or the redundant-bus assignment, but those are per-device design choices outside the scope of 1553B.
